summary.intent: Resolve greptile PR review threads on PR #584 by fixing two tombstone-path bugs: a missing 404 for non-existent/unowned/already-tombstoned names, and a missing tombstoned_at IS NULL guard in the republish sync.
summary.outcome: Both greptile fixes applied and verified (224/224 specs pass, including 3 new tombstone regression tests), committed to the feature branch.

repo: greptile-apps posts inline review threads on PRs; CodeRabbit may still be pending separately — both reviewers run independently.
NotFoundException was already imported in ipns.service.ts; IsNull needed to be added to both republish.service.ts and its spec.
The republish service spec at line 205 asserts exact TypeORM update criteria — adding a where-clause condition requires updating the spec assertion to match.
No behavioral unit tests existed for tombstoneRecord prior to this session; e2e Test 20 only covered the happy path (owned record, affected=1).

code.finding: tombstoneRecord was discarding the UPDATE affected count and returning 200 for non-existent, unowned, or already-tombstoned names — fixed to throw NotFoundException.
syncIpnsRecordSequence lacked a tombstonedAt: IsNull() guard in its update criteria, creating a race window where a tombstoned row could get its sequence bumped during republish.
Exact TypeORM update criteria assertion — must be updated whenever where-clause conditions change on the sync method.
Clean insertion point for tombstoneRecord describe block is after unenrollBatch closes; harness provides mockQbExecute and mockFolderIpnsRepo.findOne for these tests.

workflow: After creating a PR, poll for CodeRabbit review separately from greptile — both bots run independently and may land at different times.
When a spec asserts exact TypeORM criteria, a where-clause guard addition will cause a legitimate test failure that requires updating the assertion — this is expected, not a bug.
Before adding regression tests, check the spec harness (mock builder shape, available mocks) to write correct assertions rather than guessing the mock API.

friction: CodeRabbit's GitHub review was still pending when greptile threads landed — had to re-poll after resolving greptile findings.
